Fixes #8772.

body:
## Motivation

`assert_ready_eq!` expands to a `let` statement followed by `assert_eq!`, without an enclosing block. Because of that it only compiles in statement position. Using it as a match arm or as a closure body fails with "expected expression, found `let` statement", while `assert_ready!`, `assert_ready_ok!` and `assert_ready_err!` all work there.

```rust
match poll {
    Poll::Ready(()) => assert_ready_eq!(poll, ()),
    Poll::Pending => unreachable!(),
}
```

title: stream: don't panic in `chunks_timeout` with a huge `max_size`

body:
`chunks_timeout` reserves `max_size` slots each time a batch starts. If `max_size` is very large, for example `usize::MAX` to batch by time only, the first item panics, though the docs say the method only panics when `max_size` is zero. #8680 moved this reservation out of the constructor, so an empty stream works now, but any stream that yields an item still panics:

```rust
tokio::pin!(chunked);
chunked.next().await; // panics: "capacity overflow"
```

title: fs: wait for in-flight operations in File::set_permissions

labels.name: S-waiting-on-review
labels.description: Status: Awaiting review from the assignee but also interested parties.

body:
`File::set_permissions` currently spawns a blocking permission update without waiting for in-flight operations on the file to complete. Thus, wait for in-flight operations before changing permissions, matching the other `File` methods.

Having an in-flight write complete after `set_permissions` can affect the file's permissions because on Unix, `write(2)` clears the setuid (`S_ISUID`) and setgid (`S_ISGID`) bits on a file, which would undo those permission bits if `set_permissions` just set them.

body:
The current_thread scheduler and time driver currently unpark the I/O driver unconditionally on every remote wakeup and timer registration, even when the runtime thread is not parked. This causes redundant wake syscalls and leaves stale wakeup tokens in the driver that trigger spurious non-blocking park turns. Thus, track whether the current_thread scheduler is parked and only unpark the driver when transitioning out of the parked state.

Fixes: #5207
Closes: #8383
